title_en: Building the Total Portfolio at Ontario Teachers – Stephen McLennan (EP.518)
title_zh: Stephen McLennan 谈 Ontario Teachers 的整体组合构建
subtitle_zh: Ontario Teachers 联合首席投资官 Stephen McLennan 谈总组合战略、主动管理与加拿大模式的演变
summary_zh: 本期 Capital Allocators 由 Ted Seides 对话 Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan 联合首席投资官 Stephen McLennan——他参与管理这家规模约 3000 亿美元、为 346,000 名教师退休保障做配置的基金，2003 年加入后历经信用、自然资源、基础设施与总基金管理（total fund management）等岗位，2024 年与 Jillian Brown 分掌 CIO，形成加拿大最大养老基金中独一无二的双首席投资官结构。核心议题是整体组合方法（total portfolio approach, TPA）：McLennan 解释 TFM 团队如何把资产配置与财务司库（treasury）职能合二为一，以及自上而下配置与自下而上投资的平衡、主动管理、流动性（用类似 LCR 的指标衡量）与杠杆的取舍，私募股权、信用、基础设施、对冲基金与通胀敏感资产如何各得其所。他坦言参考组合（reference portfolio）的一个弊端是团队会不自觉向其权重靠拢、不愿大幅偏离；也谈到 AI 赢家带来的、长出来的集中度风险——不是简单把仓位做大，而是资产升值造成的集中，需在市场允许时克制减持。关于加拿大模式（Canadian model）的演变，他认为长期视野、可靠的合伙人履历与机构记忆仍是持久优势。
description: Building the Total Portfolio at Ontario Teachers – Stephen McLennan (EP.518)

turns.en: I'm Ted Sides, and this is Capital Allocators. My guest on today's show is Stephen MacLennan, the Co-Chief Investment Officer of the Ontario Teachers Pension Plan, where he oversees asset allocation for the $300 billion fund responsible for the retirement security of 346,000 teachers.
turns.zh: 我是 Ted Seides，欢迎收听 Capital Allocators。今天的嘉宾是 Stephen McLennan，Ontario Teachers 养老金计划的联合首席投资官，他负责管理这家规模 3000 亿美元的基金，为 346,000 名教师的退休保障做资产配置。

turns.en: Stephen joined Ontario Teachers in 2003 and worked across credit, natural resources, infrastructure, and total fund management before splitting the CIO seat with Gillian Brown in 2024, a dual CIO structure that's unique among Canada's largest pension funds.
turns.zh: Stephen 于 2003 年加入 Ontario Teachers，先后在信用（credit）、自然资源、基础设施和总基金管理（total fund management）等岗位历练，直到 2024 年与 Jillian Brown 分掌首席投资官一职——这种双首席投资官结构，在加拿大最大的养老基金中独一无二。

turns.en: Our conversation traces that path and discusses teachers' total portfolio strategy, including the balance of top-down asset allocation with bottom-up investing, role of active management, liquidity, leverage, and internal and external management.
turns.zh: 我们的访谈回顾了这条成长路径，并探讨 Ontario Teachers 的整体组合策略，包括自上而下（top-down）资产配置与自下而上（bottom-up）投资的平衡、主动管理（active management）的角色、流动性、杠杆，以及内部与外部管理。

turns.en: We cover where private equity, credit, infrastructure, hedge funds, and inflation-sensitive assets earn their place in the portfolio, how AI-driven concentration risk factors into portfolio resilience, and the evolution of the Canadian model with both enduring edges and eroding competitive advantages.
turns.zh: 我们讨论了私募股权、信用、基础设施、对冲基金、通胀敏感资产在组合中如何各得其所，AI 驱动下的集中度风险如何纳入组合的抗风险能力，以及加拿大模式（Canadian model）的演变——既有持久优势，也有被侵蚀的竞争优势。

turns.en: It coincided with the first Gulf War. As tragic as those circumstances were for the people on the ground, the connection between what was happening in the real world in terms of what was going on in CNN, how that transmitted immediately into what was going on in the markets. You could see that real-time reaction. That was the start of how I started to think about the investing world. I've done a number of different things career-wise. Each of those
turns.zh: 那次实习恰好赶上第一次海湾战争。尽管前线的人民遭遇悲惨，但你会看到：现实世界发生了什么、CNN 在直播什么、市场又怎样立刻反映——这条链条是实时可见的。那就是我开始用投资视角看世界的起点。职业生涯里我做过很多事情，每一段

turns.en: experiences has shaped me in terms of how I think about the world. What were some of those experiences and how did they shape your views? Coming out of high school, I did an undergraduate degree in business and economics and finance.
turns.zh: 经历都塑造了我看待世界的方式。（Ted）那都有哪些经历？它们又怎样塑造了你的观点？（Stephen）高中毕业后，我读了一个本科，学的是商业、经济和金融。

turns.en: My first job out of school was working for Archer Daniels Midland, which is the big U.S. agribusiness company for the Canadian operations. It involved buying and selling grain and involved logistics and involved hedging on the Chicago exchange. It was an interesting foray into the business world. It wasn't necessarily a pure investment type of role. The plan was always to go back to school to do my MBA. After my MBA, I ended up joining Merrill Lynch in their
turns.zh: 毕业后第一份工作给 Archer Daniels Midland（ADM）干，这家美国农业综合大企业，我负责它在加拿大的业务，涉及谷物买卖、物流，也在芝加哥交易所做套期保值（hedging）。那是我进入商业世界的一次有趣尝试，但不一定是纯粹的投资岗。我一直打算回学校读 MBA。读完 MBA 之后，我加入了美林证券（Merrill Lynch）的

Merrill was well positioned to do that. Combined with a lot of activity from U.S. companies coming in, buying some of the Canadian E&P entities, I got exposure to that. For personal reasons, my now wife wanted to move back to Toronto to go back to school and to be closer to family.
turns.zh: 卡尔加里办公室。卡尔加里是加拿大的能源中心，是加拿大的休斯顿，属于资本密集型行业。那份工作里有大量融资任务，美林在这块很有优势。加上当时很多美国公司跑到加拿大来收购本地的勘探开发（E&P）公司，我也接触到了这些交易。出于个人原因，我太太——现在的太太——想回多伦多，回学校读书，也离家人更近一些。

turns.en: I used that as an opportunity to think about what is the next stage of my career? How do I want to position myself to get closer to the investment process? Move away from that agent type of role as an investment banker to more of a principal type of role as an investor.
turns.zh: 我借此机会思考：我职业生涯的下一阶段是什么？我怎么把自己挪到离投资流程更近的地方？从投行那种中介型角色，转向投资人这种出资人型（principal）角色。

turns.en: Use that to go back to school. Did a mathematical finance degree here in Toronto. Then I joined teachers as a new entrant junior person. I joined the credit desk. Given my background, it was a wide mandate at the time. This would have been 2003. The credit business would have been your traditional corporate bonds, some private placements. Credit derivatives was a growing business. That was where I spent the bulk of my time thinking about how best to use
turns.zh: 于是我回了学校，在多伦多读了一个数理金融硕士。之后我作为新人、初级员工加入了 Ontario Teachers。我被分到信用部门。根据我的背景，那是一份范围非常广的职责，那是 2003 年。当时的信用业务就是传统公司债、一些私募债（private placement）。信用衍生品（credit derivatives）正在增长。我大部分时间都在琢磨怎么用好

turns.en: that product to implement whatever views we thought were appropriate at the time. The GFC was a credit derivative event. Lots of scars on my back from that particular experience. How do you deal with liquidity, counterparties, risk positioning, blocking and tackling portfolio construction was eventually elevated to be leading the credit team. It was a fantastic team.

turns.en: In 2013, the head of our capital markets group had been tasked with building a new program called Natural Resources, which was a combination of our public commodity program, which we use for its inflation characteristics, combined with an aspiration to grow a private natural resource program to be a complement to those public commodities exposures. It was a great opportunity for me to work with a new set of colleagues, work for a new boss, build a business and try to think
turns.zh: 2013 年，我们资本市场部门的负责人被安排去搭一个新条线，叫自然资源（Natural Resources）——把我们现有的公开大宗商品组合（我们主要用它来对冲通胀）和一项要做做大做强的私人自然资源投资合在一起，作为公开大宗商品的补充。对我而言，这是一次很好的机会：和新同事合作、跟新老板共事、从零建业务，试着去琢磨

turns.en: through what should that portfolio look like based on my experience prior to teachers in the energy space. We were successful in growing the private part of that program to a level on the back of some other organizational changes in terms of trying to streamline the number of programs or places where private investing was being undertaken. They moved myself and several colleagues into a renamed group called Infrastructure and Natural Resources. I had day-to-day responsibilities
turns.zh: 基于我在 Ontario Teachers 之前能源领域的经验，这个组合应该长什么样。我们把私人自然资源部分做到了一个规模，同时又赶上公司组织调整——精简私人投资条线的数量。于是我和几位同事被并到一个改名为基础设施与自然资源（Infrastructure and Natural Resources）的部门。我日常负责

In 2018, when the previous head of capital markets had been promoted to become the CIO, he asked me to come over and help him set up a new team called Total Fund Management, which has become known as this TPA concept. The thoughts around that TFM group were to combine our asset allocation function with our treasury function. I always try to explain asset allocation
turns.zh: 自然资源，同时开始熟悉基础设施团队、那些资产，以及它们怎么为整个组合做出贡献。2018 年，原来的资本市场负责人升任 CIO，他叫我去帮他组建一个新团队，叫总基金管理（Total Fund Management），也就是后来大家讲的 TPA 概念。这个 TFM 团队的想法是把资产配置职能和财务司库（treasury）职能合在一起。我总是这样解释：资产配置

turns.en: is what you want to buy, treasury is how do you pay for it. That was a great combination of my public market experience combined with my private market experience. One of the learnings that I've had over the course of my career is that public and private, notwithstanding that those two groups of market participants from time to time are different religions, don't like each other or like to debate and throw rocks at each other, they're tools to implement an overall policy view

Tim, why don't we take a step back and have you share the

There was a number of different commissions and studies undertaken. They arrived at creating an independent organization called the Ontario Teachers Pension Plan Board. A couple of key things that were important at the outset were
turns.zh: Ontario Teachers 的历史？（Stephen）我们以现在的形式在 1990 年成立。起源是这样的：80 年代，教师工会和安大略省政府——我们的联合发起人——开始担心计划的长期可持续性。他们做过好几个委员会和研究。最后决定成立一个独立机构，叫安大略省教师退休金计划委员会。一开始有几条关键原则

turns.en: independence, top-notch governance. The other requirement was to make sure that we were run as a business and had that mindset of running a world-class asset manager. The first thing that the board did was hired our founding CEO, Claude Lamarou. One of the first things Claude did was hire our founding CIO, Bob Bertram. Concurrent with that, the plan was seeded with a portfolio of non-marketable province of Ontario debentures. One of the first things Bob and Claude
turns.zh: ——独立、顶尖治理；另一条是要把自己当作一家企业来经营，以运营一家世界级资产管理公司的心态来做。董事会做的第一件事是请来创始 CEO Claude Lamoureux。Claude 上任后做的第一件事，是请来创始 CIO Bob Bertram。同一时间，计划以一批不可流通的安大略省政府债券（debentures）作为启动资产。Bob 和 Claude

turns.en: did, which was pretty innovative at the time, was use financial engineering, a derivative program to transform those non-marketable debentures into a liquid portfolio of global public equities.
turns.zh: 最早做的一件事，在当时相当创新：用金融工程和衍生品项目，把这些非流通债券换成了全球公开股票的流动性组合。

turns.en: That was the first step to this journey of diversification across a number of different asset classes. We're an early adopter of private equity, infrastructure, commodities, hedge funds.
turns.zh: 那是我们跨大类资产多元化这段旅程的第一步。我们在私募股权、基础设施、大宗商品、对冲基金上都是较早采用的机构。

turns.en: You fast forward to where we are now 35 years later. We're a $300 billion plan. We cover the retirement security of the 346,000 active retired teachers in the province. We've got a global footprint with offices in North America, in Europe, and in Asia. We've got a real track record of direct internal deployment of asset management. That's resulted in a funding ratio of 111%, which goes to the long-term sustainability of the plan.
turns.zh: 一晃眼 35 年过去了。我们现在是 3000 亿美元规模的计划，覆盖全省 346,000 名在职和退休教师的养老保障。我们在北美、欧洲、亚洲都设有办公室，有全球布局；在直接内部投放资产管理上有一份实打实的履历。结果是我们的资金充足率是 111%，这就是计划长期可持续的底气。

turns.en: Through that entire experience, public markets, private markets, TFM, now you sit today as Co-CIO. How do you lay out the current strategy at OTPP?
turns.zh: 经历过公开市场、私人市场、TFM 之后，今天你坐到了联合 CIO 的位置。你在 OTPP 是怎么铺陈当下战略的？

turns.en: Ultimately, we're trying to build a diversify portfolio that's going to be resilient across a number of different economic environments to make sure that we're in a position to honor that pension promise. I would divide that investment strategy along a couple of different dimensions, one of which would be diversification. One would be we are believers in active management.
turns.zh: 说到底，我们想建的是一个多元化的组合，能在多种经济环境里保持韧性，确保我们能兑现养老金承诺。我会从几个维度拆投资策略：第一是多元化；第二，我们是主动管理的信徒。

turns.en: Where and how do you focus your activities to deliver on that excess return? Another one would be we're focused on ensuring we've got the right risk management framework in place to deliver on that goal. The fourth one is we do use a prudent amount of leverage to execute our investment plan. Those will be the four buckets.
turns.zh: 我们聚焦在哪些领域、怎么交付那份超额回报；另一项是确保我们有一套合适的风险管理框架来实现这个目标；最后一点，我们会用一份审慎的杠杆去执行投资计划。这四块就是我们的桶。

turns.en: How do you think about the implementation of TPA or TFM? It's ultimately about delivering the best risk-adjusted portfolio with all the tools that you have at your disposal. I suppose our form of that, we probably started with a type of TPA back in 2015 or 2016 when we went down the path of a one-teacher strategy where our board before that would say, okay, management, what is the desired asset mix? Management would present to
turns.zh: （Ted）你怎么理解 TPA 或 TFM 的实施？（Stephen）说到底就是用你手上所有工具去交付风险调整后最好的组合。我们这边大概 2015、2016 年走过一条叫"One Teachers"的战略路径，就有点 TPA 的意思。在那之前，董事会会说：管理层啊，你想要的资产配比是什么？管理层就汇报给

turns.en: the board. The board would say, okay, great, that's the right asset mix. Management would then go off, try to build a portfolio to beat that asset mix. That asset mix had some characteristics of that risk portfolio. One of the challenges with that is making sure there's alignment with what you're actually trying to do. Pensions are paid with total return, not with active return or just beta return. How do you make sure that you're in a situation where everybody's aligned to deliver
turns.zh: 董事会。董事会说：好，就是这个资产配比。管理层拿回去照着这个配比去搭组合。那个配比本身带有一些参考组合（reference portfolio）的风险特征。挑战之一是确保所有人对齐到你真正想做的事上——养老金是用总回报来支付的，不是用主动回报，也不是只用 beta 回报。你怎么让所有人都在

turns.en: the best total return on a risk-adjusted basis? As we're going through that one-teacher strategy, the board said, hey, look, we're signing off on this asset mix, but it's what you folks are recommending to us. Why are we taking responsibility for that? Is there a way for you folks to be responsible for the asset mix as much as we are? That moved us down this path of having much more flexible asset mix bands. The flip side to that is that that does not mean that you don't have a
turns.zh: 一起用风险调整后最好的方式去拿总回报？在推进"One Teachers"战略过程中，董事会说：这个资产配比是我们签的，但其实是你们管理层给我们的推荐，为什么责任在我们这边？有没有可能你们和我们一样对资产配比负责？这就把我们推向了一个更灵活的资产配比区间（bands）。但硬币的另一面是——这不意味着你没有一个

turns.en: rigorous risk approach, which we do have. To me, a reference portfolio is more of a signal of risk appetite, not necessarily meant to give you a rigid portfolio construction exercise.
turns.zh: 严谨的风险方法论——我们是有的。对我来说，参考组合更多是在传递风险偏好信号，不是用来给组合搭建设一个硬框框。

turns.en: I always say, if you're going to tell me what the right risk appetite is, tell me that directly. Then it's on management and the investment team to deliver the best risk-adjusted return to achieve that consistent with all the guardrails that you would have from a risk perspective.
turns.zh: 我一直说，你要告诉我正确的风险偏好是什么，就直说；剩下的就是管理层和投资团队在风险护栏之内去交付最匹配这个风险偏好的风险调整后回报。

turns.en: Some of the downsides of having a reference portfolio is that over time, investment teams will gravitate to what those weights are. You can end up in a circumstance where, if for instance, your reference portfolio is 60% equities, 40% fixed income, investment teams will be reluctant to deviate substantially away from those weights. You can be in the world where you have a lot of fixed income exposure, like we saw in 2020-2021, where the reason for having that in the portfolio may
turns.zh: 有参考组合的坏处之一是，时间一长，投资团队会不自觉向它的权重靠。比如参考组合是 60% 股票、40% 固收，团队就会不太愿意大幅偏离。2020 到 2021 年那种环境里，你可能手上拿着大量固收敞口，但那时把它放在组合里的理由其实已经

turns.en: not be as compelling as what it once was. You end up in a circumstance where investment teams are reluctant to deviate even though they know that they should be deviating.
turns.zh: 不像过去那么强。可团队就是不愿意偏离，哪怕心里知道应该偏离。

turns.en: How do you bring it all together? Total fund management is focused on that top-down asset allocation function. How do you then layer in some of that bottom-up thinking?

turns.zh: 超额收益真正发生魔法的地方是自下而上。自上而下更多是我的地盘，Jillian 负责自下而上那一块。自上而下的杠杆里，比如：主动和被动的配比是什么？

turns.zh: 整个资产配比的杠杆和流动性配方是什么？团队花最多时间的地方，是站在更大的风险视角上把组合摆在哪里、怎么摆。这个可以做得很复杂，我们内部有很多系统在做这件事。但简单说就是：根据市场环境，我们想更激进、中性还是保守？叠加的是我们的

turns.en: risk return BOIs are to satisfy our actuarial objectives? We're a pension plant. turns.zh: 风险收益基准投资假设（BOI），用来满足精算目标。我们是养老计划，负债端的能见度其实相当清楚——尽管这笔负债可能延展 60、70、80 年。（Ted）今天这个时点，从顶层看，我们想激进、中性还是保守？怎么做出这个判断？（Stephen）我们有几个不同的规划周期和投资委员会在做这件事。第一个是我们的规划型投资流程

turns.en: which is typical of the industry, but we do run an annual investment plan where we try to think about where we want the portfolio to be over a one-year horizon. We also think about the planning process over a five-year horizon. Five years, there's nothing magic about that. It's far enough in the future where you don't have to do anything immediately today, but it's near enough that you have to start taking action today if you want to accomplish it. The five-year
turns.zh: （planning investment process），行业内很常见。我们会做年度投资计划，去思考未来一年这个组合要摆成什么样；也会做一个五年规划。五年这个数字没什么神奇的——它足够远，你今天不必马上动手；但又足够近，如果你想实现它，今天就得开始做动作。之所以用五年

turns.en: horizon is driven by the fact that we do have a portion of the portfolio that's in illiquid assets. We need to make sure that we've got the right buffer to be able to manage that because you never want to be in a position where you're a forced seller of an asset. That's why we spend a lot of time on planning out where do we think those allocations should go. We also overlay that with a rigorous liquidity and leverage system that's run by our risk team. That process of the one-year
turns.zh: 是因为我们组合里有相当一部分是不流动资产（illiquid）。我们必须确保有足够的缓冲来应对，因为你永远不希望被迫卖资产。所以我们会花很多时间去规划这些配置应该走向哪里，再叠加我们风险团队搭起来的严谨流动性和杠杆体系。一年期的

turns.en: horizon, which is probably more relevant for risk positioning, is the beginnings of how we want to structure the portfolio. A one-year horizon is still an eternity in the investment business.
turns.zh: 周期，对风险仓位更相关，是我们规划组合结构的起点。而在投资业，一年依然是漫长的一辈子。

turns.en: Within our total fund management team, there is a function which looks at more dynamic type of opportunities, how the market might be evolving, how does that compare to our original assumptions. The point of TFM isn't to be day trading the portfolio. These are big decisions.
turns.zh: 在 TFM 团队里，有一个职能专门看更动态的机会——市场可能在怎么演化，和我们最初的假设相比有什么不同。TFM 的重点不是日内交易这个组合，这些都是大决策。

turns.en: We have a group that has a specific mandate within our capital markets team, which would be frequent in nature. The TFM team and this dynamic team is there to say, look, here's what we think the environment is. Here's what we think is currently priced in or not priced into the market.
turns.zh: 在资本市场团队里，有一支小团队有专门职责，节奏上会更频繁。TFM 和这支动态团队的作用是：我们觉得环境是什么、市场当前已经反映了什么、还没反映什么。

turns.en: How should we think about a portfolio adjustment driven by a couple of things? One would be risk mitigation type of approach. If there is a particular event on the horizon that if it were to happen would be unacceptable from a return or catastrophic loss perspective, we probably would want to be thinking about that. The prototypical example of that would be going into Brexit 10 years ago. If you have a large portfolio of UK or pound-based exposure
turns.zh: 组合调整可以从两个维度考虑。一个是风险缓释——如果未来某个事件一旦发生会带来不可接受的损失或回撤，我们就会提前动。十年前的英国脱欧（Brexit）就是典型案例：你手上如果有一大块英国、英镑敞口，

turns.en: and you don't know what's going to happen, you might want to be thinking about aggressively trying to manage some of those risks. turns.zh: 又不知道接下来会发生什么，那可能就要激进地管理这些风险。另一个例子是：我们组合里某个配置，市场已经变了，重定价之后它还能不能履行原来的作用？2022 年的固收就是这样。我们当时有一笔固收配置，是按全天候（all-weather）

turns.en: philosophy. turns.zh: 哲学下配的。当收益率一直往下、几乎跌到零，我们做了大量分析。当时的 CIO 和 CEO 一起跟董事会讲：固收的预期回报已经很低，因为收益率接近零。我完全理解收益率可以为负——欧洲就是这么干过、也正在这么干。但基于央行和监管层的表态，我们判断北美出现负利率的可能性更小。固收在组合里的角色

turns.en: portfolio to be a offset or ballast to an equity shock is going to be more difficult. Why do we have this in the portfolio? There was a conscious decision to reduce our fixed income exposure that would have been driven in combination and discussion and research from that TFM group.
turns.zh: ——作为股票冲击的对冲和压舱石——会越来越难。那我们为什么还留着它？于是我们主动降低了固收敞口，这是 TFM 团队讨论和研究一起推动出来的决定。

turns.en: I'd love you to take us underneath the last time you went through your annual process, where you came out on the five-year and the one-year thoughts.
turns.zh: 你能不能带我们回到最近一次走完年度流程的那一轮？五年、一年分别落在了哪里？

Some of our peers in the US, for instance, have been aggressive in reducing what they would view as the expected return for those assets. turns.zh: 我们花了很多时间想：主动投资应该聚焦在哪些领域？一个典型例子就是私募股权的预期回报。美国的一些同行在比较激进地下调对私募股权的预期回报，我们的判断也是：私募股权在预期回报上竞争更激烈了。如果你以前能比对标资产多赚 500 或 600 个基点（bps），

We also have a team of internal investors that can also execute managing that
turns.zh: 如果现在低于这个数，那五年维度上组合该怎么反应就要认真想了。你绝对不希望自己关上一扇门——万一市场条件再变回来，你却没法部署资金，因为我们依赖合作伙伴；同时我们也有内部团队在管理这一块，

You can debate whether other people know, but we want to be balanced and not be overconfident in our ability to predict what or how that AI theme is going to evolve. The other part of it is we want to make sure that we're looking at the portfolio from this all-weather perspective and that we're not overbatting on a
turns.zh: AI 变化太快，很难有高确信的观点。我们尽量保持谦逊，承认有些事我们不知道。别人知道不知道可以争论，但我们希望自己在组合里保持平衡，不要过度自信地觉得自己能预测 AI 这条主线会怎么演化。另一部分是，我们始终从全天候的角度看这个组合，不在某一个 AI

How do you think about liquidity? You mentioned using some leverage. Those two things can go together.

Leverage and liquidity are important because what's going to get any investor into trouble and by trouble I mean get pushed out of a conviction view around where they think the portfolio should be structured would be one you have a liquidity event. You can't satisfy your near term obligations. Two is
turns.zh: 我更愿意把它拆成杠杆、流动性、资金这三件套，由我们的司库团队来管，风险团队帮我们把控这一部分组合。杠杆和流动性之所以重要，是因为任何投资人会陷入麻烦——我说的"麻烦"是被迫放弃自己对组合结构的高确信观点——无非三种：第一，你出了流动性事件，短期义务满足不了；第二，

turns.en: you lose a lot of money. The third is that you do things that your stakeholders aren't fans of. On the liquidity side, it's especially important given that we do use derivatives to complete the portfolio. We do have a rigorous process around scenario analysis and downside circumstances to ensure that we always have substantial liquidity. That's a board limit for us. We do spend a lot of time monitoring that. There's been a number of instances both in the U.S. with some of the
turns.zh: 你亏了很多钱；第三，你做的事情你的利益相关方不喜欢。在流动性这一端尤其重要，因为我们是靠衍生品去补完组合的。我们有一套非常严格的流程做情景分析和下行场景，确保任何时候都有非常充足的流动性。这是董事会层面的限制，我们花很多时间盯它。美国的一些

Brookfield combines deep operational expertise with disciplined long-term investing, uncovering value and partnering

turns.en: This is not an offer to sell or investment advice. Investing involves risk, including the loss of capital. And now, back to the show. What type of metrics do you use to calibrate the appropriate amount of liquidity?
turns.zh: 以上不构成发售要约或投资建议。投资有风险，可能损失本金。好，我们回到节目。（Ted）你们用什么指标来判断合适的流动性水平？

turns.en: We would use a LCR liquidity coverage ratio type of metric. It's not quite the same as what you would see with a bank or with a deposit taking institution because our liability structure is substantially different than a deposit based one would be akin to an LCR type of ratio customized for a pension plan. What's comfortable for you?
turns.zh: 我们用类似 LCR 流动性覆盖率（Liquidity Coverage Ratio）的指标。它跟银行或吸存机构那种不完全一样，因为我们的负债结构和存款类机构差别很大，可以看作是为养老计划定制的 LCR。（Ted）对你来说，什么程度算舒服？

turns.en: Comfortable for me is to be able to absorb a pretty substantial shock and not get pushed out of a position. It depends on what the size of the portfolio is. It has implications with currency hedging. A non-US based investor has a slightly different challenge with currencies where you're tending to hedge a illiquid long dated asset with a liquid security. You do have a maturity term mismatch. What tends to happen in a market shock is that the US dollar strengthens in this
turns.zh: 对我来说，舒服的标准是：能吸收相当大的一次冲击、不被迫离开仓位。这取决于组合大小，也和货币对冲有关。非美投资人会额外碰到一个难点：你往往要用一个流动资产去对冲一笔不流动、期限很长的资产，天然存在期限错配。市场冲击一来，通常是美元升值——在这个

turns.en: case versus the Canadian dollar. If you've done any hedging, you tend to have to post collateral against that. That would be one of the liquidity draws that would be factored into our LCR framework.
turns.zh: 语境下，就是美元对加元升值。只要做了对冲，通常就要追加保证金（post collateral）。这就是我们 LCR 框架里要计入的一项流动性消耗。

turns.en: Have you thought about where to implement active management? Where did just gain passive exposure? It comes down to where do you think you have an edge? That can be done both internally and externally. It's broader than you should just do infrastructure with external managers or internal managers. It comes down to what are the necessary ingredients for a particular strategy to be able to deliver an excess return? What were the drivers historically? What do you think
turns.zh: （Ted）你有没有想过在哪里做主动管理、哪里只做被动敞口？（Stephen）说到底就是——你觉得自己有优势的地方在哪儿？这件事可以内部做，也可以外部做。它比"基础设施该内部做还是外部做"要更广义，关键是：一个策略要跑出超额收益，必备条件是什么？过去驱动力是什么？你判断

turns.en: those drivers are going to be going forward? That active versus passive discussion, which is more of a top-down decision, paired with the bottom-up where the bottom-up deal teams will then have to say, this is where we're going to focus our activities to achieve those types of outcomes.
turns.zh: 未来的驱动力又是什么？主动还是被动——这更多是自上而下的决策；然后自下而上的 deal team 就要相应地说：我们要把精力聚焦在这些地方，才能做出那种结果。

turns.en: Did you look across your asset classes? Where have you decided to use active versus passive on one lens and then internal versus external on another if you're filling in that two by two?
turns.zh: 你们把所有资产类别拉通看过吗？一个维度是主动 vs 被动，另一个维度是内部 vs 外部，你在这个 2x2 格子里是怎么填的？

turns.en: In the equity space, passive equity versus an active public equity program has been much more challenging, at least for us. We have scale back that program. We do have a team that still does some active stockpicking. It's smaller than what it was a couple of years ago, given the fact that that's a difficult and competitive market. As we look at other asset classes, private equity, infrastructure and real estate being the big three, as well as venture. Venture introduces a
turns.zh: 股票端对我们来说，被动股票 vs 主动公开股票这条线明显偏向被动。我们已经主动缩减了那块规模，现在只剩一小支做主动选股——比几年前更小，因为这个市场又难又卷。看其他资产类别，私募股权、基础设施和地产是三大块，再加上风投。风投会带来

turns.en: different layer of complexity to the extent that those opportunities are successful. Using a hybrid model of external and internal, depending on where the market is and where we think we have competitive advantage to be able to deliver on that excess return, trying to be thoughtful around where we focus our internal resources. Where do we need to recognize that it's a activity that we're best served by going with an external partner? How do you think about the use of hedge
turns.zh: 一层额外的复杂性——一旦这些机会跑出来，情况就变了。我们用的是内部+外部混合模式，看市场走到了哪、我们觉得哪里有竞争优势去拿到超额收益，然后谨慎地想：内部资源应该聚焦在哪？什么时候要承认这块事更适合交给外部合伙人？（Ted）你怎么看对冲基金在组合里的用法？

turns.en: funds in your portfolio? Hedge funds from a top-down perspective would fall into what we call our absolute return strategies. The theoretical piece of that is have a high expected return with low correlation to some of the other major factors we have, the equity and bonds.
turns.zh: （Stephen）对冲基金——从自上而下看，它归在我们的"绝对收益策略"里。理论上的期望是：预期回报高、和我们其他主要因子（股票、债券）相关性低。

turns.en: Those are difficult to find. When you can find them, you need to be thoughtful around how are you considering the fee component of things. We do use hedge funds in that particular capacity to generate those non-correlated returns. In certain instances, if there's a certain skill set or a certain type of return stream that those individuals can deliver that we just won't be able to do internally, we are open to using that as a lever to implement our asset mix.
turns.zh: 这种机会很难找。找到之后，你就要认真考虑它带来的回报和收费是否合理。我们确实拿对冲基金做这个用途——产生非相关回报。某些情况下，如果他们具备某种我们内部拿不到的技能、能做出某类收益流，我们会把它当成杠杆来实施资产配比。

How do you go about implementing that?

From a portfolio perspective, it does introduce this tension between private

turns.en: and public investing. It's not to say that those instances didn't happen in the past with our private equity or our INR team. It wasn't as big an issue. turns.zh: 公开投资之间的张力。也不是说以前我们的私募股权或基础设施与自然资源团队没有过类似情况——只是没这么突出。我们尽量务实：一边是私人 vs 公开投资人之间的思维差异，另一边是 TVG 团队对这些标的最了解。

turns.en: As those now IPO companies become more mature, you need to start thinking about how do you best position them. turns.zh: 随着这些已上市的公司走向成熟，你要开始想怎么把它们放到最合适的团队。目前我们的判断是：让信息最充分、离资产最近的人对它负最大的责任。

turns.en: How have you thought about the position size of something as we get some of these large-scale IPOs that you didn't have control over and now you do?
turns.zh: 像你们有些大 IPO，一开始上市你控制不了仓位规模，但现在已经可以了——你在这上面是怎么想的？

turns.en: These are world-class problems when you have an asset that has become a 10, 20, 30, 40 bagger. It's a different form of problem in terms of having a concentration risk that you've grown into, as opposed to just having a large-size position. For some of these concentrated positions, we want to make sure that we're not overly concentrated as the market circumstances allow, regardless of how attractive those entities might be or what the forward-looking view might be for
turns.zh: 这是典型的"富贵病"。当一个资产变成 10 倍、20 倍、30 倍、40 倍的回报，你碰到的是"长出来的集中度风险"，不是简单的仓位做大。在这些集中持仓里，我们要确保在市场允许的情况下不要过度集中——不管这家公司多吸引人、未来展望多好

turns.en: those companies. Have you approached some of your historical areas, the credit infrastructure and resources part of the board failures? Credit is an interesting one from a top-down perspective.

turns.en: I grew up in the credit business here. I have a lot of affinity for the team there. It's got a great cash yield, can have a great sharp ratio or information ratio, has a form of risk premium from some volatility-related factor exposure. As I've transitioned to be more top-down, I recognize that it has a role for alpha generation. I'm always wrestling with the notion of credit, where from a portfolio construction perspective, when you want it to act like equity, it acts like fixed
turns.zh: 我是在这里的信用业务成长起来的，对那支团队很有感情。它有不错的现金收益，可以有漂亮的夏普比率或信息比率（information ratio），也带有一部分来自波动率相关因子暴露的风险溢价。但我转向更自上而下之后，我认识到它在 alpha 生成上是有角色的。我一直在纠结的一点是：从组合搭建的角度看，信用在你希望它表现得像股票时，它表现得像

turns.en: income. When it's a positive growth environment and equities are putting up big games, by construction, you're capped. The other challenge with credit is that then when you want it to act like fixed income, it acts like equity. It also has these other characteristics that depending on how extreme the overall macro environment is, you might be getting something that you don't want or need in the portfolio. What you described on credit is negative skew. How do you take that lens and decide
turns.zh: 固收；当增长环境好、股票大涨时，你在结构上就被封顶了。信用的另一挑战是：当你希望它表现得像固收时，它反而像股票。它还带其他特征——取决于宏观环境多极端，你可能得到一份组合里并不想要、并不需要的东西。（Ted）你描述的信用其实是负偏度（negative skew）。你怎么用这个视角去决定

turns.en: how you want to implement that in the portfolio? We're fortunate that we have a wide scope of activities in the fund. Any one program is part of a bigger portfolio. How is it affected and how does it contribute to the overall portfolio? Another observation that I've had is diversification is a powerful portfolio tool. In any given period, it's likely to make you unhappy.
turns.zh: 在组合里怎么落地？（Stephen）我们幸运的地方在于组合的活动范围很宽，任何一条配置都是大组合的一部分——它怎么受影响、又怎么为大组合做贡献？我另一个感受是：多元化是一个很强的组合工具，但任何一段时间里，它常常让你不开心。

turns.en: Most investment committees will look at the line item of all the asset classes or all the securities. We'll then gravitate to the things that are above the line and say, these are really great. The things below the line, the natural reaction will be, why are we doing that? You need to put in the context of what was the expected contribution of those things above the line and below the line? How do they interact? That's another way to
turns.zh: 大部分投委会都会看每一条资产类别或每只证券。线以上的会让我们觉得真棒，线以下的我们自然反应就是"为什么还留着"？你得把它们放回原来的框架里：线以上的和线以下的，各自预期贡献是多少？彼此又怎么互动？这也是一种表达

turns.en: express that diversification. How do we think each of these components is going to contribute to our overall objective to deliver a risk adjusted return? How do you layer that on to the risk reward and credit where it doesn't act the way you would like in different environments?
turns.zh: 多元化的方式：我们怎么判断每一条会怎么贡献给"以风险调整后回报实现总体目标"这个使命？（Ted）把这个视角再叠加到信用的风险回报上——它在不同环境里可能不是你希望的那种表现——你怎么办？

turns.zh: 我们用一个相当简单的增长 vs 通胀的坐标系。你从这里开始想：未来的环境大概长什么样？信用在低波动环境里表现确实好。

turns.en: Other asset classes might not be performing quite as well. That's why I'm torn from a asset allocation perspective because in a big set of outcomes, it's going to perform well.
turns.zh: 其他资产类别可能就没那么好。所以资产配置上我挺矛盾的：因为在一大部分情形里，它会表现不错。

turns.en: How do you think about those tail outcomes? What other parts of the portfolio do you need to be providing offsets to what might be going on for this particular asset class?
turns.zh: 那些尾部结果你怎么想？组合里还需要哪些部分来对冲这一资产类别可能出问题的情况？

turns.en: One of those offsets would be infrastructure. I would love to hear how you've gone about implementing the infrastructure piece. We've been in infrastructure on the direct side since 2002-2003.
turns.zh: 其中之一就是基础设施。（Ted）我想听你讲讲基础设施这块你们怎么落地的。（Stephen）我们从 2002、2003 年就直接做基础设施投资。

turns.en: We were an early adopter of the asset class. Infrastructure has some interesting characteristics and it's loosely consistent with our overall risk profile. It's been a great contributor to the overall fund for the last 20 plus years. Our implementation has been to do that direct with the team. Those assets tend to be more scalable than what you might see in some other areas.

turns.en: We've had a team in place not only here in North America but in Europe, in Asia that's been out there looking at those opportunities. It does provide that stability of cash flows and that exposure to that real rate, which is quite attractive when we're thinking about the overall portfolio. turns.zh: 我们不仅在北美有团队，在欧洲、亚洲也有团队一直在外面找机会。它确实提供了现金流的稳定性和对真实利率（real rate）的敞口，在我们思考整体组合时非常有吸引力。（Ted）当我们看整个组合时，内部 vs 外部管理的资产比例大概落在哪里？

turns.en: There's no preset number. We try to be thoughtful and pragmatic that in certain instances, partners, in this case, GPs, are we getting good value for fee? In many instances, we do.
turns.zh: 没有预设数字。我们努力做得审慎、务实：某些情况下，合伙人——这里就是 GP——我们要判断我们付的费换回来的价值划不划算。很多时候，我们是划算的。

turns.en: It depends on the market. It depends on how we feel. Our own internal capabilities are going to be able to execute on an appropriate risk return type of construct. There's no preset rules.
turns.zh: 这要看市场，也要看我们对自己内部能力的判断——能不能做出一个合适的风险回报结构。没有预设规则。

turns.en: We would want to be thoughtful and flexible and not be in a situation where it needs to be a specific number that drives you to bucket filling, which can never be a good event.
turns.zh: 我们要保持审慎和灵活，不要让某个"具体数字"反过来驱使我们去凑仓位——凑仓位从来不会是什么好事。

turns.en: What's the range of the proportion of external managers that you've had over time? Each group will have a different allocation and it also depends on the maturity level.
turns.zh: （Ted）外部管理人比例的历史区间大概是多少？（Stephen）每一条配置都不一样，也取决于成熟度。

turns.en: The ratio is anywhere from 10% to 30% on the external side. When you look for an external manager, what does that process look like? We have dedicated teams, both private equity and other groups that are focused on those fund relationships. They would be going through a more typical origination funnel around what or where we're trying to bulk up our expertise or our exposures. They would go through a market
turns.zh: 外部这块大致在 10% 到 30% 之间。（Ted）当你们找外部管理人时，这个过程长什么样？（Stephen）我们有专门团队——私募股权和其他部门都有专门做基金关系的人。他们走的是更常见的 origination funnel，看我们在哪个方向上要补专业能力、补敞口。他们先做一轮市场

turns.en: screen, think about what the environment is in whatever sector or geography we're talking about, then would go out, meet partners and then start thinking about the appropriate way to allocate capital. What are some of the common characteristics of partners that you gravitate to?
turns.zh: 筛选，看你说的这个板块或地区的环境是什么；然后出去见合伙人，再去想以什么方式配置资本最合适。（Ted）你们愿意靠近的合伙人一般有什么共同特征？

turns.en: First and foremost, it's having a partner that wants us to be a partner with them. That's important in terms of them being able to recognize that we can be more than just capital partners, but also be contributors to how they're thinking about their various businesses.
turns.zh: 首先——得是一个愿意和我们做合伙人的合伙人。这一点很重要，因为这意味着他们能认识到我们不只是资金方，还可以对他们各个业务线怎么想问题做出贡献。

turns.en: We also want to make sure that we're getting the return that we need for the fees that are being paid. I'd love to talk about the structure of your team. Maybe start at the top, this dual CIO structure, which isn't something you hear a lot about. How do you come together to make decisions?
turns.zh: 同时我们要确保交的那笔费拿回我们需要的回报。（Ted）我很想聊聊你们的团队架构，也许可以从最上层的双 CIO 结构开始——这不是一个常见的安排。你们俩怎么一起做决策？

turns.en: We do have this close CIO role, and that was on the back of the resignation of the prior CIO. We took that as a chance to think about what would be best for the future. The fund's grown considerably over the last 35 years. The number of asset classes has grown. The number of investors that are within the investments group has grown substantially. The world's become a lot more complex. We made the decision to go with the dual CIO model, but we're clear that we each have our
turns.zh: 我们是 co-CIO 这个安排，是在上一任 CIO 辞职之后决定的。我们把它当作一个机会去重新思考：未来最合适的架构是什么？过去 35 年基金长大了很多，资产类别变多，投资团队里的人大幅增加，世界也复杂得多。我们做了选择：双 CIO。但我们心里非常清楚，各自负责

turns.en: own domain and accountabilities. I'm responsible for the asset allocation. My colleague, Jillian Brown, is responsible for the public and private investing function. We've worked together for quite some time, so we're very familiar personalities to one another. Where we have a more formal overlap, in addition to oversee the overall portfolio, is that the regional offices report into me, and one of the prime objectives of our regional offices is to deliver active returns.
turns.zh: 自己的领域和责任。我负责资产配置，我的同事 Jillian Brown 负责公开与私人投资这一块。我们一起工作很久了，非常熟悉彼此的性格。除了共同监督整个组合之外，一个更正式的交叉点是：区域办公室向我汇报——而区域办公室的一个首要目标就是交付主动回报。

turns.en: An easy example is that we have two major investment committees. We have a total fund investment committee, which would be those broader asset allocation functions, stocks, bonds, commodities. Matt is chaired by me. Jillian is a member of that committee, and she will be able to provide context to me either in the meeting or outside of the meeting.
turns.zh: 一个简单的例子是：我们有两个主要投委会。一个是总基金投委会，涵盖更宏观的资产配置——股票、债券、大宗商品——由我主持，Jillian 是成员，她可以在会上或会前会后给我补充背景。

turns.en: We have another investment committee called the public and private investing committee. Matt is chaired by her. I'm a member of that. Matt's responsible for the oversight of our large public and private investments. Those are the more formal structural parts of the fund.
turns.zh: 另一个是公开与私人投资投委会，由她主持，我是成员，负责监督我们的公开和私人投资大宗交易。这些是组合结构上更正式的一部分。

turns.en: Other things that we'd use to make sure that we're managing the portfolio effectively is we have weekly meetings with our CEO and CRO, where any of those edge items or decisions that are closer to use the concept of economic indifference, where there's not necessarily a right answer, there's some need for debate and discussion. The other part of this is making sure that we are constantly communicating with one another. Ultimately, it comes down to a level
turns.zh: 还有一些确保我们管好组合的机制：我们和 CEO、CRO 每周都开例会，把那些边缘议题、或者按"经济无差异"（economic indifference）概念上——没有唯一正确答案、需要辩论讨论的决定，都放到这个桌上聊。另一个部分是我们俩之间始终在沟通。说到底，这建立在一个层面

turns.en: of trust and respect for each other's domain so that we don't end up with a major conflict when we're trying to make some of these key decisions. If there was a major issue, we would ultimately go to our CEO to help us arbitrate, but that hasn't been an issue to date.
turns.zh: 上——彼此的信任和对对方领域的尊重。这样我们在做关键决策时才不会演变成大的冲突。真出现大问题，我们最终会找 CEO 仲裁——到今天为止还没有。

turns.en: What's an example of some of the more interesting conversations you've had on one or both of those investment committees of late? There's been a number of transactions that we've looked at on the private side across a number of sectors where we're trying to be thoughtful around the disruption risk for these businesses. AI generally, it's difficult to have high conviction.
turns.zh: （Ted）最近一两次投委会上，有哪些有意思的讨论？（Stephen）私人端我们看过不少交易，跨很多行业，我们都在努力想清楚这些企业面临的颠覆风险。AI 这条主线本身就很难有高确信。

turns.en: We're in the investing business. That's part and parcel with making decisions under uncertainty, but there's been a lot of discussion and debate on that side. At the total fund level, recently it's related to overall risk positioning. As you look at that today on that lens of conservative, neutral, aggressive, how are you feeling about the world?
turns.zh: 我们本来就是干投资的，在不确定性里做决策是这份工作的应有之义。但那一边确实有很多讨论和辩论。总基金层面，最近的话题更多围绕整体风险仓位。（Ted）以今天的眼光看——保守、中性、激进——你眼里的世界是哪一种？

turns.en: It's a tricky world out there. We're probably of the view that we're best positioned to be a bit more in that neutral range. The challenge is that that can change. We try to be thoughtful and have a big debate about where or how we should be thinking about the overall portfolio positioning. As you look over the course of history, how often have you been in that neutral category compared to one of the ends? The bulk of the time you probably are in the neutral category,
turns.zh: 这个世界挺难琢磨。我们的判断更偏中性一点。挑战是它可以变。我们尽量审慎，也会在整体组合摆位上做大的辩论。（Ted）从历史看，中性这一档和两端相比占多大比重？（Stephen）大部分时间你其实都落在中性，

turns.en: given the fact that markets are pretty good at pricing. My observation is that market efficiency is on average there efficient. There's always pockets where things are overpriced and other areas where they're underpriced. Generally, the starting point is that they're probably fairly priced, then you need to be quite selective. How do your internal and external investment teams share information and work together? That's something that we have spent a lot of time on over
turns.zh: 因为市场在定价上其实相当在行。我的观察是，市场效率在平均意义上是有效的——总有地方被高估、总有地方被低估，但起点是"它们大概率被公平定价"，然后你要非常挑。（Ted）内部和外部投资团队怎么共享信息、怎么配合？（Stephen）这是我们过去

turns.en: the last 10 or 15 years in terms of making sure we've got good information flow across those two groups. In some instances, they're more integrated. That is something that you need to focus on in terms of regular dialogue between those internal individuals, also making sure that there's the right connectivity between the direct teams and those funds. What are the areas where you found there to be more synergy between the internal and external teams? In some of the
turns.zh: 10、15 年来花了很多精力去做的事——确保这两拨人之间有良好的信息流。有些条线上，两边整合得更紧，需要内部人员之间有常规对话，也要确保直投团队和那些基金之间有正确的连接。（Ted）哪些地方你发现内外团队协同效应更强？（Stephen）在一些

turns.en: hedge fund spaces, we do have some large public market strategies that the partners in those spaces are true collaborators and have great dialogue with our internal teams in terms of challenges that we might have with how are we structuring a certain part of the portfolio?
turns.zh: 对冲基金领域，我们有一些体量比较大的公开市场策略，那边的合伙人真的是我们的合作方，会和我们内部团队就"我们这一段组合的结构怎么摆"这些具体问题有非常好的对话。

turns.en: How do we think about liquidity? How do you use things like AI? You mentioned the regional offices reporting to you. What are those offices tasked with? For background, we have a team in Europe that would cover multiple sectors. It would include infrastructure. We have a venture group there. We have real estate investors there and we have private equity investors there. In Asia, we have a team in Singapore as well as a team in Mumbai. Those areas of focus would be more
turns.zh: （Ted）我们怎么想流动性？怎么用 AI 这类东西？你提到区域办公室向你汇报，他们被派了什么活？（Stephen）简单背景：欧洲有一支团队，覆盖多个板块——基础设施、风投、地产、私募股权都在里面；亚洲在新加坡和孟买各有一支队伍。他们的重点区域更偏

turns.en: infrastructure, private equity and venture. We don't have a forced allocation by geography. We want to be opportunistic and make sure that we're using that diversification lever.
turns.zh: 基础设施、私募股权、风投。我们没有按地理硬性分配，希望保持机会主义，把多元化这根杠杆用起来。

turns.en: Those teams are tasked with going out, finding sourcing and asset managing value out opportunities in those respective markets in those respective asset classes.
turns.zh: 这些团队的任务就是在当地市场、当地资产类别里找 sourcing，找从资产管理里 value out 的机会。

turns.en: How did you think about the reporting lines of people on the ground looking at assets? We have been operating under a matrix model which requires both the asset class as well as the regional head to be supportive of a transaction to make sure that we're combining what is good for the overall portfolio with local knowledge that the deal teams in those regions are meant to bring. I'd love to ask you about the evolution of the Canadian model and the 20-something years
turns.zh: （Ted）当地看资产的人汇报线怎么设计？（Stephen）我们一直用矩阵模式，一笔交易要同时得到资产类别负责人和区域负责人支持，以确保我们既从整体组合的角度出发，也用上了那些区域 deal team 应该带来的本地知识。（Ted）我很想聊加拿大模式的演变——你在 Ontario Teachers 待了 20 多年

turns.en: you've been inside of teachers. What do you see as the remaining competitive advantages of the model? Independence of governance, diversification, varying degrees of internal management. 20 years ago, there was not a lot of folks that had those characteristics and had the pool of capital to be able to execute on those particular items. Fast forward to today, there is a lot more that would have a similar set of characteristics. The competition or the uniqueness of where we were
turns.zh: 。你怎么看这个模式剩下的竞争优势？（Stephen）治理独立、多元化、以及不同程度的内部化管理——20 年前具备这些特征、同时又有足够资金去执行这些事的机构没几家。今天具备类似特征的机构已经多了很多。我们 20 年前的独特性和竞争位置

turns.en: 20 years ago is substantially different. Some of the advantages would be we do have a long-term horizon. Now, that might not be differentiable versus another pension plan, but it is a difference versus a GP or another entity that might have a fixed life and has to do certain things with their portfolio. We have a long track record of being a good partner and being in a position to be able to deliver on whatever we say we're going to deliver on. The third item that does position
turns.zh: 已经完全不同。但一些优势还在：第一，我们是长期视野——跟另一个养老基金比可能差别不明显，但跟有存续年限、必须对组合做一些事情的 GP 或别的主体相比，那就是差别。第二，我们有长期做一位好合伙人、说到做到的履历。第三，把我们摆在很好位置的是

turns.en: us quite well is that we do have that institutional memory. We have all the processes in place, board governance, back office, middle office, deal professionals that all can execute. Sometimes that gets taken for granted when I speak to some of the peers in the US, elsewhere in the world.
turns.zh: 我们的机构记忆——所有流程都在那里：董事会治理、后台、中台、deal professional 都能落地执行。我跟美国或世界其他同行的朋友聊时，这一点常常被当成理所当然。

turns.en: That is something that they're like, oh my goodness, you got to build out all this infrastructure. We have that already. Another advantage that we have is one single cohort of beneficiaries.
turns.zh: 他们常常说：天哪，这一整套基础设施你得从头搭——而我们早就有了。我们另一个优势是只有单一一批受益人。

turns.en: That allows us to build one portfolio with that portfolio being fully aligned across that group. There's a real affinity for our mission. Most people in their life have had a positive experience with a teacher. That acts as a great way for us not only to attract partners, but also to recruit and retain staff. The biggest one for the Canadian peer group is that we tend to be well-funded. In our case, we've got a funding ratio of 111%. People get into trouble,
turns.zh: 这让我们可以只用一个组合，就能对齐所有受益人。我们的使命天然让人亲近——大部分人一生中都被一位老师善待过，这也是我们吸引合伙人、招募并留住员工的好抓手。对加拿大同业来说最大的优势是：我们通常资金充足——我们是 111% 的资金充足率。投资人出麻烦

turns.en: our investors get into trouble when they're forced into a risk spot that they're not comfortable with. That's when mistakes get made. We can be the master of our own destiny, pick where on the risk curve we want to play based on where we think the best market opportunities are.
turns.zh: 往往是被迫坐到自己并不舒服的风险位置上，错误就是这么发生的。我们可以做自己命运的主人，基于我们看到的最佳市场机会，选风险曲线上的哪个位置去玩。

turns.en: When you take into account that fully funded status, how do you think about the objectives of continuing to grow the pool compared to maintaining the fully funded status?
turns.zh: （Ted）考虑到完全资金充足这个状态，你怎么权衡"继续把资金池做大"和"维持充足率"这两个目标？

turns.en: It would be up to the sponsors. I don't want to overstep my role in this particular item, but we spend a lot of time thinking about where would you be optimally risked and how do you think about that as the funding ratio changes. That allows us to focus on what our actuarial return is, make sure that we're delivering on that to ensure pension solvency.
turns.zh: 这得由发起人决定。我不想越位——但我们花很多时间想：随着充足率变化，最优的风险水平落在哪里。这样我们可以专注于精算回报，确保我们兑现它、维护养老金的偿付能力。

turns.en: Where does that shake out in terms of a number? Our stated objective on a risk-adjusted basis is to deliver 7% nominal on a consistent basis.
turns.zh: （Ted）落到数字上大概在哪里？（Stephen）我们公开的、风险调整后的目标是持续交付 7% 的名义回报。

turns.en: What are some of the ways in which the early advantages of the Canadian model no longer exist? The ability to write a large check and get preferential deal terms with whoever the vendor of those, that is definitely eroded. There's been the broader increase in competition for many of these assets. More competition just means compressed expected returns. That's not necessarily unique to the Canadian model. That's a phenomenon that we've seen across all markets as
turns.zh: （Ted）加拿大模式早期的优势有哪些已经不复存在？（Stephen）"下大额支票就能拿到优惠条款"——这条已经被削掉了。很多资产上的竞争在加剧，竞争多就意味着预期回报被压。这不只是加拿大模式独有，是所有市场随着更多资本涌入

turns.en: more capital has flown in. The ability of that capital to access private asset returns or alternative returns has compressed excess return premium. How do you think about the strengths, in some cases, the disadvantages of your size? The strength of our size gives us scope across a number of different opportunities. We're not forced into one particular set of activities. It also helps with attracting and retaining staff in terms of being able to offer, do you want to be a good
turns.zh: 都能看到的现象。这些资本能进入私人资产或另类资产回报，把超额回报的溢价压薄。（Ted）你怎么看你这个规模的优势、以及某些情况下的劣势？（Stephen）规模给我们的好处是"范围"——我们可以横跨很多种机会，不会被绑在某一类活动里；规模也帮我们吸引和留住员工，因为我们可以提供一个选择：

turns.en: investor and hone all your skills across the investment lifecycle? That would include origination, asset management, execution, also across asset classes. I'm the case in point, I've done a number of different things, internally, public, private, putting it all together. The size of the business and the scope and scale of the business contributes to that aspect of things.
turns.zh: 你想不想做一个"好投资人"，在整个投资生命周期里把各种技能打磨出来？包括 sourcing、资产管理、执行，也跨资产类别。我就是这样一个例子：我在内部做过很多事，公开、私人、把它们串起来。业务的规模、广度和深度支持了这一可能性。

turns.en: What are some of the most top-of-mind investment topics that you're wrestling with? When you think of how the world's changed since COVID, let's use that as a delineation point, big themes. One would be heightened cost of capital, could be because of higher inflation, higher risk-free rates generally transmitting into higher required returns across a number of different asset classes. The second one would be related to geopolitics that used to be
turns.zh: （Ted）眼下你脑子里最放不下、最纠结的投资话题是什么？（Stephen）如果用新冠作为分水岭看世界的变化，我觉得有几个大主题。第一个是资本成本的抬升——可能因为通胀更高、无风险利率更高，传导到各类资产的必要回报。第二个是地缘政治，过去主要围绕

turns.en: predominantly focused on US China in terms of how those two great powers were going to think about and evolve through the next 5, 10, 15, 20 years. That's evolved into being a bit broader of late.
turns.zh: 美中这两大强国未来 5、10、15、20 年会怎么相处。最近这块已经变得更广。

turns.en: The third category would be technology, specifically AI. Those would be the three big things that we're trying to think about. How are those going to affect our overall portfolio?
turns.zh: 第三个是技术，尤其是 AI。这就是我们一直在琢磨的三件大事——它们会怎么影响我们的整体组合？

turns.en: How are they going to affect the growth profile? How are they going to affect the inflation portfolio? How do we need to adjust now to make sure that we're still in a position to have a robust portfolio, recognizing that the range of outcomes have become significantly wider in our opinion over the last couple of years? If you look at your 5-year projections over each of those lens, cost of capital, geopolitics, technology, how are you trying to adjust the portfolio to best position
turns.zh: 它们会怎么影响增长？怎么影响通胀？我们现在要做哪些调整才能有一个稳健的组合——毕竟在过去几年里，我们认为结果范围明显变宽？（Ted）如果沿着你这三个视角——资本成本、地缘政治、技术——看五年预测，你打算怎么调组合

turns.en: for those changes? For each of them, we try to come at it with a degree of humility and say, what is the general direction of impact on growth and inflation? How is that going to interact with the various parts of the portfolio? I don't know if there are specific areas that I would want to comment on that, hey, look, we think that AI is going to lead to a giant productivity shock. That's going to be good for asset prices generally. I would hesitate to be
turns.zh: 让它们最匹配这些变化？（Stephen）每一条我们都努力带着一点谦逊去看：增长和通胀被往哪个方向推？它们跟组合的各个部分怎么互动？我不太想具体评论哪一块，比如"我们认为 AI 会带来一次巨大的生产率冲击，那对资产价格整体是好事"——这种判断我不敢

turns.en: overconfident in making those projections. We don't have high conviction on many of these items. Let's make sure that we're running a balanced portfolio and that we've got the right set of scenarios in place to ensure that we don't end up in a circumstance of having a big drawdown in our face. What are the most important initiatives from teachers over the next couple of years? The big one is ensuring that we've got the right handle on how do we use AI as a business
turns.zh: 做得太自信。很多事我们并没有高确信。我们只想确保组合是平衡的，情景集是合适的，不要有朝一日一个大回撤摆到脸上。（Ted）Ontario Teachers 未来几年最重要的举措是什么？（Stephen）一个大事是：作为一家企业，我们怎么把 AI 用对——

turns.en: in terms of making sure we've got the right tooling for people and ultimately are using that technology to get to better decisions. That's what the real prize is here. There's obviously productivity enhancements. To me, it's how do you make sure you're using the access to all this information and the way that AI can analyze and manipulate that information to get to better decisions? Stephen, I want to make sure I get a chance to ask you a couple of closing questions.
turns.zh: 确保我们有合适的工具给人用，最后用这个技术做出更好的决策——这才是真正的奖励。生产率的提升当然是显而易见的，但对我来说，关键是：你怎么把对信息的可得性，加上 AI 分析和加工信息的能力，用来做出更好的决策？（Ted）Stephen，我想在结束前再问你几个收尾问题。

turns.en: What is the most rewarding thing you do outside of work? It's a pleasure to be the CIO of this institution to be a steward of capital for the 346,000 teachers in Ontario. It is quite busy.
turns.zh: （Ted）工作之外让你最有成就感的事是什么？（Stephen）能在这家机构做 CIO、替安大略省 346,000 名教师当资本的管家，是我的荣幸。但确实非常忙。

turns.en: Spending time with friends and family is pretty important. In the winter, I love snowboarding. In the summer, we're very fortunate to have a cottage. Spending times outdoors and fishing.
turns.zh: 陪朋友和家人非常重要。冬天我喜欢滑雪板（snowboarding），夏天我们很幸运有一个湖畔小屋（cottage），能去户外、钓鱼。

turns.en: What was your first paid job and what did you learn from it? In high school, I had the typical jobs in retail, lifeguarding. My first paid job would have been as a newspaper delivery boy for the Ottawa citizen. We had to show up every day, even though it probably only took 30 minutes or thereabouts. As I tie into my experiences and credit, the other aspect of being a paper boy was accounts receivable collection, because after you delivered the newspapers, you'd have to go back
turns.zh: （Ted）你第一份拿钱的工作是什么？你从里面学到了什么？（Stephen）高中时我做过典型的零工——零售、救生员。第一份拿钱的工作是给 Ottawa Citizen 送报。我们每天都得出工，虽然可能半小时就搞定。说到这，跟我后来在信用那边的经历呼应——送报童的另一份活是应收账款，你把报纸送到之后要挨家

turns.en: and collect every couple of weeks, the $3. Surprisingly, there was always a couple of houses that nobody was home, even though you could see that the TV was on. That was a lot of fun and a real lesson. Which two people have had the biggest impact on your professional life?
turns.zh: 去收那 3 美元，每两三周一次。神奇的是，总有那么几家人——明明家里电视在开，但就是没人应门。那是一段很有意思的经历，也是一堂真实的课。（Ted）哪两个人对你职业生涯影响最大？

turns.en: From my experience in Calgary as an investment banker, one of my bosses was Chris Burley. Chris was an incredibly bright, incredibly hard worker. He had a real knack which I still tried to emulate to this day around preparation for whatever meeting or whatever session negotiation used a useful exercise of game-thearing out or war-gaming out what the opposite side might be thinking about. The other piece would be I'd been fortunate. I've worked for all the CEOs,
turns.zh: 我在卡尔加里做投行的时候，我一位老板是 Chris Burley。Chris 极度聪明，也极其勤奋。他有一个本事——直到今天我还试着学——就是对每一次会、每一场谈判都做扎实的准备工作。他用一个非常好用的练习：把对方可能的想法"博弈推演"一遍（war-gaming）。另一件幸运的事是我给历任 CEO、

turns.en: all the CIOs of teachers since inception. Each of them have sprinkled certain things and made impressions over time. Perhaps to coming to recency bias, which I know that you're not supposed to, I would want to give a shout out to Joe Taylor, our CEO, and Jillian Brown, my co-CIO, who have provided a support network not only on the investment side, but also on some of the broader issues as it relates to people or other areas of the overall puzzle of running a business.
turns.zh: 历任 CIO 都做过事，从成立那年开始。每一位在不同时间往我身上洒过一些东西、留下过一些印记。可能会有近因偏差——我知道不该这样——我想特别感谢 Joe Taylor，我们的 CEO，还有我的 co-CIO Jillian Brown，他们给了我一个支持网络，不只是投资端，还包括跟人、跟经营一家企业里其他拼图有关的更广泛的问题。

turns.en: Honorary mention would be to Ziad Hindo, who was the prior CIO, who was a great investor and had a great impact on me. One of the things that he always said and still sticks with me is that you need to do what you think is right for the portfolio. Even if some people are going to disagree with you, you need to believe in what you're doing. That has stuck with me and is certainly something that I've tried to maintain as I think about the portfolio now.
turns.zh: 还要致敬一下 Ziad Hindo，上一任 CIO，他是一位非常出色的投资人，对我影响很大。他常说的一句话直到今天还跟着我：你要做你觉得对组合最有利的事——哪怕有人不同意，你也要相信自己正在做的事。这一点我一直记着，也是我今天思考组合时努力保持的原则。

turns.en: Steven, last one. What life lesson have you learned that you wish you learned a lot earlier in life? Earlier in my career, I had a lot of fear of missing out in terms of, hey, look, why did that individual get that particular opportunity or that job or that promotion? One piece of advice that I have gotten, which I wish I had learned earlier, was related to be thoughtful and think about what you think the next stage of your career is or what the next role is that you want to have.
turns.zh: （Ted）Stephen，最后一个。你有什么后悔没早点学到的人生教训？（Stephen）我职业生涯早期很 FOMO——总觉得为什么那个人得到了那个机会、那份工作、那次晋升？一个我希望自己早点学到的建议是：用心想一想——你的下一阶段职业生涯是什么、你想要下一个岗位是什么。

turns.en: That could be to get more technical knowledge. It could be to develop your leadership skills. As other opportunities come along, don't get too stressed out if that particular role doesn't fit that opportunity. If you look at it that way and you say, hey, look, my peer just got this particular role and you might feel, oh my goodness, I wish I had that. Then you reflect on it and say, well, look, I don't even want to do that. Why am I getting all uppity about it?
turns.zh: 可能是让你获得更多技术知识，也可能是锻炼领导力。当别的机会出现时，如果那个岗位跟你想去的方向不匹配，不要过度焦虑。你换个角度想：同事拿到了那个岗位，你心里痒痒的——"天哪，我也想要"；但你回头一想，其实我根本不想干那份事，那我为什么情绪这么大？

turns.en: Steven, thanks so much for sharing this great overview of teachers. Thank you for having me. Thanks for listening all the way to the end. If you made it this far, how about one ask for me?
turns.zh: （Ted）Stephen，非常感谢你给大家这么完整地讲了 Ontario Teachers。（Stephen）谢谢你邀请我。（Ted）也谢谢你听到这里。如果你听到了这里，我有一件小事请你帮忙好吗？

turns.en: Tell one friend about the show. It's the best way to keep growing this incredible community. Thanks so much. And until the next one, stay curious and keep compounding knowledge, relationships, and capital a little bit at a time.
turns.zh: 把你的朋友介绍给我们。这是让这个小共同体继续长大的最好方式。非常感谢。下一次节目之前——保持好奇，一点一点让知识、关系和资本持续复利。
